title: Switchboard — Logic Circuit Workbench
description: Wire gates, flip-flops and seven-segment displays on a live board, then read the truth table and timing scope it writes for you.
concept: Switchboard is a digital-logic bench in one page. Drag parts from the rail, pull wires between pins and the simulator settles the whole board 24 times a second — signals light up and flow along the wires as you flip switches. Cross-coupled gates really hold state, so an SR latch latches and a D-flip-flop ripple counter counts on a 7-segment display. Any circuit you build gets its truth table swept automatically and its signals plotted on a 260-tick logic scope, and you can take it with you as JSON, a PNG or a share link.
features: Eleven part types — switches, clock, AND/OR/XOR/NOT/NAND/NOR, D-flip-flop, LED and a hex 7-segment display
Live event-settled simulation with animated signal flow, feedback latches that actually hold state and one tick of ripple delay per flip-flop
Automatic truth-table sweep over every switch combination, with clickable rows that drive the board
260-tick logic scope with per-signal traces and an adjustable clock rate
Seven built-in circuits: half adder, full adder, SR latch, XOR-from-NANDs, 2-bit counter, hex counter and a 2-to-4 decoder
Export the board as PNG, download the circuit as JSON, or copy a share link that carries the whole design in the URL
localStorage autosave, pan/zoom/fit, erase tool and touch-first pointer handling

interaction.mouse: Drag parts to move them on the grid, drag empty board to pan, wheel to zoom.
interaction.click: Tap a switch to flip it, tap a palette chip then the board to place a part, tap a truth-table row to drive the inputs.
interaction.touch: Everything is pointer-based — tap to toggle, drag to move, drag pin to pin to wire; the palette scrolls horizontally.
interaction.keyboard: Delete/Backspace removes the selected part, Space pauses or resumes the simulation, Escape drops the active tool.
